candidate_profile.description: The candidate is strong and commercially grounded. They focus on revenue, compare store geographies well, diagnose the product mix mismatch, and give a strong recommendation, though with slightly less polish and synthesis than a truly excellent answer.
behaviour_rules: Begin with a concise recap and explicitly note that the problem likely sits on the revenue side because backend cost savings are already in place.
Ask relevant questions about store profitability variation, geography, consumer behavior, and competition.
Structure the problem clearly around differences between metropolitan and suburban stores.
Quickly rule out competition as the main differentiator once the case evidence points elsewhere.
Identify that all stores carry the same mix and use that clue to investigate customer demand differences.
Clearly connect suburban profitability to higher sales of major appliances and electronics, which are higher-margin products.
Conclude that urban stores are carrying inventory and using floor space inefficiently because the assortment is not well matched to urban demand.
Recommend customer-level analysis, differentiated assortment, and selective closure of stores that cannot sustain the lower-value mix.

expected_issues: May not be quite as hypothesis-driven or executive-ready as a fully excellent candidate.
Could be slightly less crisp when synthesizing the final recommendation and implementation trade-offs.
expected_feedback_points: Clear comparison of metropolitan and suburban store economics.
Correct identification of customer behavior differences and product mix mismatch.
Strong recommendation to tailor assortment and review underperforming stores for closure.
To reach excellent level, make the final synthesis even tighter and more board-ready.
